description: Owner-approved numeric claims outside the treatment architecture (Stage 9.48). A figure in a member-facing file is explained by an entry here only when the entry's market, owning resource, context patterns and label requirement all match the sentence it appears in. Treatment figures are NOT here: admin-import/config/treatment-sources.json owns them, and the scanner defers to it. Figures inside an owner-approved safety block are covered by that block's own recorded sources in safety-blocks.json.
status: SEEDED 2026-09-23 (Stage 9.48), Bucket C cleared 2026-09-23 (Stage 9.49) — REPORT-ONLY. Blocking mode is not enabled.
seedingRule: Seeded only from Bucket A: figures whose source is recorded in approved stage work. Nothing is seeded from memory, nothing from Bucket C, and no citation is invented.

claims.allowedWording: at least three litres of drinking water per person per day, for at least three days (nine litres per person)
limitations: This is the NZ emergency baseline for drinking and basic hygiene. It is not an Australian figure and must not appear in an AU file.
Get Ready says to store more where you can: heat, hard work, children, nursing mothers, illness and pets all increase it.
Some parts of New Zealand could be without water for longer; the local emergency management committee advises.

claims.jurisdiction: QLD (state-specific, used as a labelled example)
claims.allowedWording: Emergency guidance such as Get Ready Queensland advises storing at least 10 litres of drinking water per person for three days, and your state or territory emergency service may advise more for your area.
limitations: A state example, not a national Australian rule: the wording must keep 'your state or territory emergency service may advise more'.
It is not a New Zealand figure and must not appear in an NZ file.

claims.jurisdiction: QLD (state-specific, used as a labelled example)
claims.allowedWording: Get Ready Queensland advises storing drinking water for three days. Check your own state or territory emergency service for the advice that applies where you live.
limitations: Queensland guidance, and the attribution must stay in the sentence: it is not a national Australian figure and must never be called 'the Australian' or 'the national' baseline.
Scoped to OG-08. The same three-day figure for food in OG-11 is a separate claim with its own entry.

claims.jurisdiction: QLD (state-specific, used as a labelled example)
claims.allowedWording: food for at least three days (Get Ready Queensland), shown beside NSW's up-to-14-days figure to make the variation plain
limitations: Queensland guidance about food, not water, and not a national Australian figure.
It appears beside the NSW Food Authority figure precisely so that neither reads as national.

claims.jurisdiction: NSW (state-specific, used as a labelled example)
claims.allowedWording: supplies for up to 14 days (NSW Food Authority)
limitations: State guidance shown beside the Queensland figure precisely to show that Australian advice varies; neither may be presented as national.

claims.allowedWording: The official emergency baseline in New Zealand is food for at least three days (Get Ready).
limitations: A minimum, and NZ only: Get Ready says to store more where you can, and the Australian figures are state-level and different.

value.text: 1 litre per square metre per millimetre of rain

claims.allowedWording: Every square metre of roof catches about 1 litre of water per millimetre of rainfall, before losses.
claims.authority: Building Performance, MBIE (and the definition of a millimetre of rain over a square metre)
limitations: It describes what lands on the roof, not what is collected: the wording must keep 'before losses' and the statement that what lands on the roof is not what you can use.
No collection efficiency is approved — there is no published standard figure.

value.text: 1 litre per square metre per millimetre of rain

claims.allowedWording: Every square metre of roof catches about 1 litre of water per millimetre of rainfall, before losses.
claims.source: arithmetic: one millimetre of rain over one square metre is one litre
claims.authority: definitional — no jurisdictional source is claimed for Australia
limitations: Recorded separately from the NZ entry on purpose: the conversion is arithmetic, but no Australian authority is cited for it, and none is implied.
Same wording rule: 'before losses', and no efficiency figure.

value.text: 240 L rain barrel; 500 L+ garden tank; 5,000 L indoor supply with year-round rain; 10,000 L+ with dry summers; at least 30,000 L as a sole supply

claims.allowedWording: NZ published planning guidance (Building Performance, MBIE) — examples for each use, not requirements or OffGrid056 recommendations
limitations: Published planning guidance and examples, each tied to the use it belongs to (garden, indoor supply, sole supply). Not requirements, and not OffGrid056 recommendations.
NZ only. No Australian figure exists and the AU file carries none.
Owned by OG-10: repeating them in another resource would turn a labelled example into a rule (Stage 9.45 decision for OG-B08).

value.text: 150 m² roof × 1,000 mm rain = about 150,000 litres before losses

claims.allowedWording: Worked example, not your figure: a 150m² roof where 1,000mm of rain falls in a year catches about 150,000 litres before losses.
claims.authority: definitional, labelled as an example in the resource
limitations: The label is part of the claim: it must stay 'Worked example, not your figure', and it must keep 'before losses'.
No collection efficiency is approved, so this is what lands on the roof, not what a member can use.

value.text: 150 m² roof × 1,000 mm rain = about 150,000 litres before losses

claims.allowedWording: Worked example, not your figure: a 150m² roof where 1,000mm of rain falls in a year catches about 150,000 litres before losses.
claims.authority: definitional, labelled as an example in the resource
limitations: As the NZ entry. No Australian authority is cited, and none is implied.

claims.jurisdiction: NSW (state-specific, used as a labelled example)
claims.allowedWording: closely fitting, fine insect-proof screens on all inlets and overflows — NSW Health gives about 1 mm as an example
limitations: NSW guidance, and an example: it may not be presented as a national Australian requirement, and it may not appear in an NZ file.
It is a screen aperture. It does not approve '1 mm' of anything else — a clearance, a gap or a tolerance.

claims.allowedWording: a stand over 30cm and under one metre; a tank on a stand over one metre high generally needs a building consent
limitations: A consent threshold and a stand description, not a structural design: the base and the stand stay with the manufacturer, the supplier and a qualified professional.
NZ only. No Australian equivalent is published, and the AU files carry none.

value.text: about a kilogram per litre — a full 1,000-litre tank is about a tonne

claims.allowedWording: water weighs about a kilogram per litre, so a full 1,000-litre tank is about a tonne (MBIE)
match: \ba litre of water weighs a kilogram\b
claims.authority: Building Performance, MBIE ('Because a litre of water weighs a kilogram…')
limitations: A conversion so a member can ask the right question of a supplier. It is **not** a design figure: no slab, footing, reinforcement or load specification may be derived from it in the resource.
The 1,000-litre tank is an illustration, not a recommended size.

value.text: about a kilogram per litre — a full 1,000-litre tank is about a tonne

claims.allowedWording: water weighs about a kilogram per litre, so a full 1,000-litre tank is about a tonne
claims.source: arithmetic: one litre of water has a mass of about one kilogram
claims.authority: definitional — no Australian authority is cited, and none is implied
limitations: As the NZ entry: a conversion for asking the right question, never a design figure, and the 1,000-litre tank is an illustration rather than a recommended size.
Maintenance of a tank, not a treatment or testing interval — testing intervals belong to the treatment registry.
NZ only: no Australian household interval is published, and the AU file carries none.
